The core combat mechanics feel good, but the game is unacceptably broken. There are a couple of really good bosses that I enjoyed a lot, but most are somewhere between barely bosses, and so bad I can't believe they made it into the game in the state that they are in.

Here is a great example of the game not being ready for prime time. If about a third of the time that you die, your souls just don't spawn to give you a chance to be pick them up, your game is not ready to ship. That is THE souls mechanic in a souls-like, and if you can't do that extremely basic core mechanic consistently, go make something else please.

I do have a feeling that if the devs keep working to fix the insane amount of bugs and revamp some of the extremely boring fights, like the final boss, this could be a great game in 6 months. Until then play a better, less broken video game.

For full price can't recommend. Get it when it's half off.

The crashing can be fixed! 
Great game, great story. This remaster is known for crashing constantly due to lack of VRAM, which I was able to fix by doing this:
Go to C:\Users\user here\AppData\Roaming\BioshockHD\Bioshock2. (This folder will only show up after the game has been launched at least once.)
Open the file Bioshock2SP.ini with a text editor, search for "TextureStreamingMemoryLimit" and change the value from 256 to something like 2048 (or higher, depending on how much VRAM your graphics card has, but 2048 worked fine for me). This is the number of MB allotted for the game on your graphics card.

Hopefully 2K will make this an automatic fix in the future!

Genuinely fantastic game. The level design is incredible, the enemy design is varied and combat encounters force you to consider how best to approach them. Puzzles make you stop and think, and feel extremely satisfying to finally solve. The boss design is great as well, and the abilities all feel VERY juicy to use.

Not only that, the music... OH, the music. Some of the best properly 8-bit tunes I've heard since Shovel Knight, and it's clear that's where the inspiration comes from. The art is gorgeous as well, and I've had to just stop and stare several times while I was playing.

In short: If you like metroidvanias, or the older Zelda games, or just think unrealistically gigantic swords are cool, PLAY THIS GAME. At only 20 bucks Canadian it's practically highway robbery.

A short game masterfully crafted by ISART students (Out of Seats Studio). It features a beautiful art style, a great atmosphere, enjoyable gameplay, and excellent engine optimization.
I even increased the ResolutionQuality value in the GameUserSettings.ini on purpose, and the game still showed no major frame rate drops. That is a clear sign of solid optimization, which has become quite rare these days. It's especially worth highlighting because the game runs so well without relying on DLSS or FSR. On top of that, it supports native ultrawide out of the box!
Truly impressive work! Congratulations to the entire team! I can't wait to see what you create next.

Unfinished Business is exactly what a DLC should be. It's focused, badass, and worth the admission price. Clocking in at around 9 hours of content, this expansion doesn’t just tack on filler; it expands on the best parts of Rogue City with more grit, more story, and more RoboCop. You’re back in the titanium boots of Alex Murphy, and it feels just as satisfying as ever. The writing is sharp, the atmosphere remains soaked in that gritty 80s Detroit aesthetic, and the voice acting continues to deliver the perfect mix of nostalgia and cybernetic. The devs put real love into this. It's not a cash grab; it’s a solid continuation that respects the fan base. If you enjoyed Rogue City, this DLC is a no-brainer.

It's Skyrim in a world that looks like Elden Ring, without the souls like difficulty. That's really all that needs to be said, because that's exactly what it is.

Highly recommended.
Edit: 4k/120fps with literally everything set as high as it can go and DLSS quality at 70%. Lowest frame rate ever dropped was 114 and that was during a fight with five summons vs about six enemies.. Zero issues with optimization for me.
